To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multiple FGF8 isoforms, which are expressed in developing limb structures, activate receptor splice forms which are expressed in mesoderm.

the FGF8 gene is expressed as multiple isoforms in developing limb and face, that each isoform interacts with a unique subset of fibroblast receptors, and that this interaction may be important for growth or patterning in the developing embryo.
FGF-8 is alternatively splicing to produce at least 7 isoforms, and that these isoforms interact with different fibrobast growth factor receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of fibroblast and epidermal growth factors in development.
the identification of genes that are expressed in the developing limb.
the role of fibroblast factors in the patterning and growth of the mouse embryo, and in the development of human cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FGF8b and Fgf8c activate FGFR3 and FGFR4 and FGF8b also activates FGFR2.

the FGF receptor family consists of four distinct receptors, FGFR1-4, each encoded by a separate gene, and each containing three or more alternative splice forms (FGFR1a, 1b, 1c; FGFR2b, 2c, 2d; FGFR3b, 3c, 3c2; and FGFR4b, 4c).
the FGF receptor splice forms expressed in the mesenchyme of developing limbs and craniofacials regions are activated by the FGF- 8b and Fgf-8c isoform proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FGF-8 is expressed in the ectoderm and is secreted into the surrounding mesenchyme.
FGF-8 can be divided into at least 7 distinct isoforms, which are expressed during mouse development.
FGF-8 can be expressed by different tissues in different developmental contexts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FGF8 isoform is a very important signal for the development of the limb bud and the craniofacial skeleton.
the FGF8 isoforms that are expressed in the developing limb are likely to interact with FGFR2 and FGFR3 splice forms.
the FGF8 isoforms activate different fibroblast receptors in the developing mouse embryo, and that the FGF receptors are spliced differently in different tissues.
